narration.text: Mr Hasan is awake, but a breathing tube means he can't say a word. So here, he is the ventriloquist. The phone only moves its lips, and it says nothing he hasn't confirmed.
A nurse clamps a phone to the bed rail, and Mr Hasan picks a movement he can still make. Eyebrows up means yes. Muse Spark names the movement, and SAM 3.1 learns to follow it.

First, Muse Spark reads the room: what the nurse just said, the family photo he keeps looking at, the visitor who left ten minutes ago. Each clue can only nudge the odds, and each one shows where it came from. Then the phone asks the one question that narrows things most. SAM 3.1 tracks his eyebrows, and a second, blind Muse Spark judge checks every answer.

But the room is empty, and he can't press a call bell. So his words chime at the nurses' station and stay there until someone taps "I'm coming". If nobody does, the phone says them again and the alert gets louder. The WhatsApp message to Aisyah waits for a nurse's approval too.

Now an agent takes over. It watches the message reach Aisyah's phone and get read. When she answers, Muse Spark reads the reply first. Anything about his health waits for a nurse. This one doesn't, so he hears it.
Wrong guesses happen. He says no and spells it: three letters, and the completer finds "kucing", cat. The message: who is feeding my cat?
Three quick yeses, at any moment, raise the alarm on every screen.
Under the hood it's Meta's stack: Muse Spark from calibration to the blind judge, SAM 3.1, Voice Transcribe, and Muse Wonder for memory.
Privacy mode runs the same pipeline on Muse Spark Open, the open-weight model, on Baseten. Patient video never reaches a closed API.
